field_definition: full citation, DOI/ISBN/catalogue identifier where available, and publication type
example_values_or_taxonomy: journal_article, book, book_chapter, PhD_thesis, preprint, conference_paper, grey_literature

field_definition: primary and secondary disciplinary framing of the study
example_values_or_taxonomy: hermeneutics/philosophy, digital_humanities, history, archival_science, computer_science/NLP, statistics, political_science/game_theory

field_definition: the kind of source material the study itself analyzes, if any
example_values_or_taxonomy: VOC_archive, EIC_archive, other_colonial_archive, literary_corpus, oral_history, none_theoretical_only

field_definition: time period and geographic scope of the study's own subject matter
example_values_or_taxonomy: free text, e.g. '17th-century Southeast Asia', 'contemporary NLP benchmark'

field_definition: the study's own stated research question(s)
named interpretive/hermeneutic theory invoked, if any
example_values_or_taxonomy: e.g. Gadamer, Ricoeur, distant/close reading, none_stated

field_definition: named computational or statistical method, if any
example_values_or_taxonomy: e.g. Hawkes process, NER pipeline, ERGM, none_computational

field_definition: whether and how the study formally separates a latent process from its observed/recorded trace
the study's unit of analysis
example_values_or_taxonomy: e.g. document, event, actor-dyad, sentence, corpus-year

field_definition: what the study claims to estimate or interpret
denominator used for any reported proportion/rate, if applicable
how (if at all) the study validates its method
how uncertainty is represented, if at all
how source-to-claim provenance is tracked, if at all
role of human judgment in the study's method, if any
how the study treats interpretive ambiguity/plurality of meaning
how the study treats colonial classification and archival silence
whether/how the study addresses identifiability of its model
how the study treats null/negative/failed-validation results
availability of code, data, or replication materials
limitations as stated by the study's own authors
relevance to S1, Atlas, Model 3B, Hawkes, networks, game theory, or counterfactual work
example_values_or_taxonomy: S1_bibliographic_identity, Atlas_ontology, Model_3B_Hawkes_relevant(H_i^relevant), Model_3B_general, network_analysis, game_theory, counterfactual, none_directly
